In the peculiar circumstances of this case where  the complainant himself has stated that he is satisfied  with the settlement amount and has no objection if the FIR  2  and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed, it is  unlikely that the present FIR will result in a conviction  when the complainant himself does not wish to pursue the  case.
In such a case, this Court is of the opinion that no  purpose would be served by keeping the dispute alive and  the continuance of the proceedings would amount to abuse  of the process of Court.
I am of the opinion that this is  a fit case to exercise discretionary jurisdiction under  Section 528 of the BNSS.
4. What has, in fact, transpired is that the complainant who received the settlement amount, as noted in the paragraph extracted above, was the first vendee of the property in dispute.

It is,
however, not in dispute that the very same property subsequently sold to the appellants, who claim to be b purchasers.
Significantly, no settlement has been arrive between the appellants and the vendor against whom the FIR was lodged.
In these circumstances, the settlement entered into between the first vendee and the vendor cannot bind the appellants.
The quashing of the proceedings in their entirety effectively renders the appellants remediless, save and except when their claim can be satisfied in civil proceedings.

5. That being so, we partly allow the instant appeal impugned judgment of the High Court quashing FIR No.57 registered under Sections 420/34 IPC at Police Station Civil Lines,

The Trial Court shall proceed further in accordance with law in relation to the FIR lodged pursuant to which a chargesheet has already been filed.
The respondents shall be at liberty to avail such remedies as are permissible in law.
3 6. As a result, the pending interlocutory application also stands disposed of.
